audience: adults who have meant to 'sort this out' for years and never found a first step small enough to take (listing: audience[0], problemsSolved[0])
people saving 'in case of emergency binder', 'if something happens to me file' and 'life admin binder' ideas, who abandoned a printable binder at tab 2
parents of young children working out who would raise them and who is named on the pension or life cover
people named as an executor, or adult children trying to find a parent's will and accounts (guides: named-executor-what-you-agreed-to, talking-to-your-parents-about-their-affairs)
anyone after a move, marriage, new baby, job change or separation who knows their paperwork is now out of date
pet owners and people with dependants who want one note that says who steps in
privacy-minded planners who will not write passwords in a binder and want 'where, not what'

visualWorld.setting: A calm study desk in daylight: cream paper on a warmer cream ground, a navy cloth-bound book called My Affairs, a ring binder, a filing box, a key ring with manila tags, a home safe and a bank deposit box. Everything is about where things are and who to ask, never the thing itself: tags carry names and places, never numbers or codes.

props.draw: Upright rectangle in ink navy #26374f with a slightly darker spine strip on the left (8% of width), a thin cream rule two-thirds down, the title 'My Affairs' in Newsreader serif in cream, and a brass #9a7b3f ribbon bookmark (narrow rectangle with a V-notch at the bottom) hanging out of the top edge. Matches the real cover in creative/public/screens/personal-life-affairs-companion-printables.png.

One horizontal plank (warm cream #e4ded0, 24px tall, darker under-edge line) with 4 to 6 plain spines of varying height and width in muted creams and greys (#cfc8b6, #e2dccd, #565c68 at 30%), no titles. The emergency-book stands among them, pulled half out or leaning at 8 degrees so it is the only coloured object.

Two cream #fbf8f1 pages side by side with a shallow centre gutter shadow; left page carries an eyebrow in small caps ('START HERE'), a serif heading and a hairline rule; right page lists 5 to 7 short lines with right-aligned section labels in navy, separated by dotted leaders. Real text only (see pins).
Binder opened flat seen from above: left board navy, three brass ring circles on the spine line, right board holding a cream page. Tab dividers stick out of the right edge in a staggered column.

Rounded-corner rectangles stepping down the binder's right edge, alternating cream #fbf8f1 and slate #e6eaf0 with a navy 2px outline, each with a short real label in IBM Plex Sans. An absent tab is simply absent (a gap), never crossed out.

Long cream envelope (ratio 2.2:1) with a V flap outline and a brass circle seal on the flap point; the word 'Will' handwritten-style in navy (a plain serif italic, not a script font). Optionally a manila-tag tied to it.

Portrait cream sheet tilted -4 degrees with a navy header bar, 6 to 8 grey ruled lines, small sans field labels taken from the guide ('Named beneficiary', 'Account'), and ONE line highlighted with a brass-soft #f6efe0 highlighter stroke (rounded rectangle, 70% opacity) under a name line left as a plain rule. A paperclip (two nested rounded U strokes) on the top edge. No real or fake personal names.
Circle or rounded rectangle outline in navy at 60% with inner ring, slightly rotated; carries a real phrase only (e.g. 'Still true', '12 months'), never an invented date.

A brass split ring (two concentric circles, 3px stroke) hanging from a small hook, with 2 or 3 flat keys (circle bow with a hole, straight shank, 3 to 4 square teeth) and manila tags on short string lines.
Luggage-tag shape (rectangle with the two top corners clipped) in #f1e6c8, a reinforced hole ring at the top, string as a thin curved navy line; carries 1 to 2 lines of real text in Plex Sans.
Long shallow metal box seen from the front: slate-grey rectangle with a hinged lid line, two keyholes (circle plus small trapezoid) side by side, a small plain nameplate rectangle with no number.
Squat cube front: navy-grey square with a rounded inner door, a dial (circle with tick marks only, no digits) and a short handle bar. Optionally a manila-tag on the handle.
Small chest-shaped box in slate with a carry handle on top and a single latch; a folder edge peeks out from the lid line.
Open banker's box seen at 3/4: cream body, handle cut-out, hanging folders with staggered tabs labelled with real area names.

Rounded-rectangle phone, navy frame, slate screen with a padlock glyph (rounded body plus arch) and a row of 6 empty circles for a passcode, deliberately blank. A manila-tag on a string tied to the phone carries the real step label.

Three overlapping square photo frames with thick white borders, each holding a flat landscape (two hills and a sun circle) or a simple two-figure silhouette, plus a cloud outline (three arcs on a base line) behind, and a small shoebox lid. No faces.

Sitting cat or dog silhouette in navy built from circles and a rounded body, a brass collar with a round tag, and an index card (cream rectangle with a red-free top rule) propped beside a food bowl (half-ellipse).

Vertical stack of 4 to 6 rounded cards (cream, 1px #cfc8b6 border) joined on the left by a dotted brass line through numbered navy discs (1, 2, 3...). Each card has a person glyph (circle head over a rounded-shoulder shape) or a small object glyph, a bold short label and one muted line.

Horizontal ruler-like band in slate #e6eaf0 with tick marks and three labelled marks ('12 months', '24 months', '36 months'), small paper cards resting on it that flip from cream to brass-edged when confirmed.

Round navy-outline stamps, each with a simple glyph: a house roof (I moved), two interlocked rings (I got married), a split circle (I separated or divorced), a pram (I had or adopted a child), a briefcase (I changed jobs), a key in a door (I bought a place), a laptop (I started working for myself), a paw (I no longer have a pet); labels are the exact LIFE_EVENTS labels.

The app's own step card as a flat illustration (not a screenshot): cream #fbf8f1 card with a 1px #e2dccd border and soft shadow, a navy ribbon bookmark at the top right, a small-caps area eyebrow, a large Newsreader question, a muted hint line, and answer pills. Text copied exactly from captures.ts or affairsKnowledge.ts.
Pill buttons in a row or stack: outlined cream pills for options, one filled navy pill; labels are the real choices from captures.ts (e.g. 'Yes', 'No', "I'm not sure").

Rounded navy device frame holding one of the real screenshots from creative/public/screens/personal-life-affairs-companion-*.png, cropped from the top, shown at 300 to 380px wide. Only used where the screenshot actually shows that pin's subject.
Small brass circle with a cream tick. Spent only on something confirmed or done, as the product itself does (document.tsx: brass marks confirmation).

visualWorld.palette: The product's own ink and paper: ink navy #26374f (strong #1a2738), cream ground #efebe2, paper #fbf8f1, deeper cream #e4ded0, slate wash #e6eaf0, text #1b1f27, muted #565c68. Brass #9a7b3f with brass-soft #f6efe0 is the single warm accent and only marks something confirmed, highlighted or done. Manila #f1e6c8 is allowed for tags. No sage/teal and no red/black: definition.ts notes those are what Pinterest's results for this kind of product already look like, so navy on cream is the open seat in that feed.
visualWorld.mood: Calm, orderly, quietly reassuring: a well-kept study on a weekday morning. Respectful, never morbid: no candles, lilies, gravestones, hourglasses, black backgrounds or 'when I die' imagery. Objects are tidy and findable; people appear only as simple glyphs, never faces.

archetypes.name: The Book on the Shelf
archetypes.clicks: This niche sells printables, and sellers' guidance is consistent that mockups showing the printable in use, and previews of different pages, lift click-through (expertbeacon.com, dodopayments.com). This product's output is literally a printed book, so a book you could take off the shelf is the honest mockup. The shelf also answers the niche's most-asked follow-up, 'where should I keep it' (somewhere private but findable).
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500 on cream #efebe2. 60-130: small tag and subtle Draftpace mark top-left (never lower-right, which Pinterest's own UI covers). 140-470: headline in Newsreader, navy, 64-84px, max 3 lines, left-aligned with 80px margins. 500-1120: the visual, a shelf plank at y=1080 running edge to edge with plain spines and the navy My Affairs book pulled out or leaning (closed variant) OR the book lying open showing a real page (open variant, pages 760px wide). 1150-1340: one real line or 2 to 3 short real items on a paper card. 1370-1470: product line (name and real price from the listing, or 'Free guide').
archetypes.visual: bookshelf with plain spines and the navy My Affairs emergency-book with brass ribbon; open variant shows the open-book-page with real text.
archetypes.text: Headline; on the book or page only real strings: 'My Affairs' (document.tsx), the 'If you need to.' page with HANDOFF_SCENARIOS needs and AFFAIR_AREA_LABEL section names, or a real sentence from the pin's description, the listing or the guide.
archetypes.bestFor: The printable book, opening page, how to keep the file, starting with your own, the 'if something happens to me file' itself.

archetypes.name: Inside the Binder
archetypes.clicks: The dominant format in this niche is the 'what to include' section list: emergency and death binder guides are organised by section (frugalconfessions.com, newlynamed.com), retail 'If I Die' binders sell on their section count (walmart.com listing with 16 sections), and multi-step reference content is what people save to come back to (schedulala.com). Showing the tabs is the visual form of that list.
archetypes.layout: Cream ground. 70-120 tag. 130-400: headline, navy, 62-78px. 430-1300: ring-binder opened flat, rotated -3 degrees, occupying 860px width; tab-dividers stepping down the right edge carry the real labels (up to 8); the right page shows the same labels as a contents list with dotted leaders and a one-line 'what goes here' for the first two tabs. Gaps where a tab does not apply. 1330-1470: product line.
archetypes.visual: ring-binder with tab-dividers; variant: an executor's folder (filing-box) with paper-clipped sheets for the executor guide.
archetypes.text: Tab labels and contents copied from the guide table 'The eight tabs, and what to leave off each' (life-admin-binder-what-goes-in-it), AFFAIR_DOMAIN_LABEL / AFFAIR_AREA_LABEL in affairsKnowledge.ts, or the guide list being visualised.
archetypes.bestFor: What goes in a life admin / ICE binder, the 'skip what does not apply' angle, the executor's 'what to ask for' list.

archetypes.name: The Line on the Form
archetypes.clicks: A single recognisable document, large and centred, survives Pinterest's grid crop and reads at thumbnail size (marpipe.com: keep the product large and centred; Pinterest's text-overlay advice: short, legible, high contrast). The beneficiary-vs-will fact is a 'did you know' surprise, and a highlighted line on a form makes that surprise visible without words. Inference from the research, not a measured result.
archetypes.layout: Top band 0-560 in ink navy with the headline in cream Newsreader 66-80px (60-500), tag above it. The beneficiary-form (or will-envelope) is laid on the cream lower half, 560-1300, tilted -4 degrees and overlapping the band edge by 60px so the paper reads as 'pulled out'. One line on the form highlighted in brass-soft; 3 to 4 real table rows printed on the sheet. A will-envelope tucked behind at +6 degrees. 1330-1470: product line.
archetypes.visual: beneficiary-form with highlighted name line, will-envelope, paperclip; for medical decisions, three overlapping sheets labelled with the guide's three terms.
archetypes.text: Headline in the navy band; on the paper only real rows from the guide tables (beneficiary-forms-override-your-will, emergency-contact-and-medical-decision-maker) or the product's book labels (AFFAIR_STEPS bookLabel).
archetypes.bestFor: Beneficiary forms, will vs form, health care proxy, guardian naming, paperwork after divorce.

archetypes.name: Where, Not What
archetypes.clicks: Most binder printables in this niche include a passwords log (the search results list 'a passwords log' among standard printables), while digital-legacy and binder guides warn against writing passwords or combinations down (TechHappy digital legacy PDF; the binder guides' own caveats). A pin that shows the object with a tag saying who can open it, not the code, is the trustworthy contrarian tip and matches exactly what the product records. Object close-ups also hold up in the grid.
archetypes.layout: Visual first, headline lower, so it looks different from the others. 0-900: the object hanging or standing centre-frame on cream (key-ring from a hook at y=0, or a home-safe / deposit-box / phone-lock / pet), 600-760px wide, with 2 to 3 manila-tags each carrying one real line. 930-1230: headline, navy, 60-76px, left-aligned. 1240-1330: one real line in muted sans. 1370-1470: product line.
archetypes.visual: key-ring with manila-tags, home-safe, deposit-box, fireproof-box, phone-lock, photo-stack, pet-with-note, will-envelope with tag.
archetypes.text: Tags carry real prompts, hints, placeholders or field labels from captures.ts (e.g. 'A name, not a code. Never record the combination here.') or a real guide line. Never a number, code or password, even a fake one.
archetypes.bestFor: Safes, deposit boxes and spare keys, phone access, photographs, pets, where the will is kept and who knows, where to keep the binder.

archetypes.name: In This Order
archetypes.clicks: Step-by-step 'how to' is what most top-performing pins have in common (Tailwind's analysis of top pins), and sequenced checklists are what people save (schedulala.com). In this niche specifically, executor kits sell on a dated order: a 'First 90 Days' map and a notification log (payhip.com executor binder listing).
archetypes.layout: Cream ground. 70-120 tag. 130-390: headline, navy, 60-76px. 420-1320: contact-chain of 4 to 6 numbered cards down the left 700px with a dotted brass connector; each card a bold short 'who/when' plus one muted line; a single supporting prop (phone, will-envelope, filing-box) at the right edge, 220px wide, at the height of card 1. 1350-1470: product line.
archetypes.visual: contact-chain with numbered discs and person/object glyphs; optional calendar-strip ticks for day-based timelines.
archetypes.text: Ordered items copied from a guide timeline or ordered list (e.g. where-to-look-for-a-will 'The search order', who-to-tell-when-someone-dies table, hospital guide timeline) or from HANDOFF_SCENARIOS. May be cut after the first clause, never reworded.
archetypes.bestFor: Who to tell and in what order, where to search for a will or accounts, the hospital two-week test, the guardian checklist, the handoff check.

archetypes.name: One Question at a Time
archetypes.clicks: Product pins do best when they show the real product in use (expertbeacon.com on preview images; Pinterest's own guidance for product sellers favours showing the product clearly). This product's difference from every binder in the feed is that it asks one question at a time, so the honest product shot is one real question with its real answer choices: it reads like a quick self-check, which invites the save.
archetypes.layout: Slate wash #e6eaf0 ground (the only archetype not on cream, so shop pins are recognisable). 70-120 tag. 130-360: headline, navy, 58-72px. 400-1120: question-card at 820px wide, rotated -2 degrees with soft shadow: ribbon bookmark top-right, area eyebrow, question in Newsreader 52px, hint in muted 26px, answer-chips row. 1000-1400: phone-frame with the real screenshot overlapping the card's lower-left corner ONLY when the screenshot shows that subject; otherwise a second smaller card with the follow-up prompt. 1370-1470: product line with the real price.
archetypes.visual: question-card, answer-chips, phone-frame (real screenshot where it matches).
archetypes.text: The exact prompt, hint and choices from captures.ts CAPTURE_SPECS, the instruction/bookLabel/minutes from AFFAIR_STEPS, the intake question and its 'why' from INTAKE_QUESTIONS, or LIFE_EVENTS labels. Area eyebrow from AFFAIR_AREA_LABEL. The card is drawn as an illustration, never passed off as a screenshot.
archetypes.bestFor: Every shop-linked pin about a specific step: will location, executor authority, medical decision maker, emergency contact, recovery kit, accounts that charge money, intake questions, life events, safes.

archetypes.name: Still True?
archetypes.clicks: Every emergency-binder guide in the research says to review it at least once a year or after a big change (frugalconfessions.com, newlynamed.com, protective.com), and the most common failure of a binder is staleness. A pin about time passing, with life-event stamps, answers the saver's quiet worry that a binder is out of date the moment it is finished, which is also this product's distinctive feature.
archetypes.layout: Cream ground. 70-120 tag. 130-430: headline, navy, 62-78px. 470-820: calendar-strip across the full width at y=640 with labelled interval marks, life-event-stamps sitting on it and 3 small paper cards above the marks. 860-1000: two pills side by side, 'Still true' (brass outline, brass-check) and 'Update it' (navy filled). 1040-1320: 2 to 5 short real lines (e.g. what each event brings back). 1370-1470: product line.
archetypes.text: Interval labels from confirmEveryMonths in AFFAIR_STEPS (12, 24, 36 months), button labels from WorkspaceModule.tsx ('Still true', 'Update it'), event labels from LIFE_EVENTS (lifeEvents.ts) and the guide table 'Where to look again, by event'.
archetypes.bestFor: Keeping it current, life changes, the old form left on a first day, still-true reviews.
